title.rendered: I Wanna Start a New Life

content.rendered:
Today’s entry is another abandoned work-in-progress, but it’s one that showed a lot of promise.

This home demo of recording of “I Wanna Start a New Life” dates back to late 1979, likely after Bruce had finished his ultimately abandoned The Ties That Bind album, but before the second batch of sessions that produced the songs that would ultimately round out the two-disc The River.

We only have two verses (of which two lines are completely bluffed) and a chorus to figure out what Bruce was reaching for, but we also have a gorgeous acoustic melody that sounds for all the world like something Jackson Browne might have recorded.

We left our home on the hillside
We left our family and our friends
We came down here to ???
To start all over again

We left when the fields turned for springtime
We went down there in eight hours time
Da da da da da da
Da da da da da

I wanna start a new life
I wanna start a new life
I wanna make it easy and free
And forget about the man that I used to be

That last line likely gives away the game: had Bruce completed the song, it’s likely that “I Wanna Start a New Life” would have fit neatly into one of Bruce’s favorite themes–a search for escape, redemption, and second chances.

Unfortunately, though, Bruce doesn’t seem to have pursued the song any further, so “I Wanna Start a New Life” never had a chance at any life at all.

I Wanna Start a New Life
Recorded: Late 1979 (demo only)
Never released
Never performed

© March 2, 2021

excerpt.rendered: This gorgeous Jackson Browne-ian work-in-progress ballad might have made for a gorgeous song had Bruce completed it.

jetpack-related-posts.title: I Don’t Wanna Be
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This melodic ancestor to "Jackson Cage" captures The Big Man standing just a bit too close to the mic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Everybody Wants My Baby
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "Everybody Wants My Baby" was on its way to being an edgy uptempo rocker before it went missing in action. Listen to a pretty well-formed demo inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: I Wanna Marry You
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This early love song hasn't aged well but it paved the way for Bruce's more mature and nuanced reflections on love and marriage.

jetpack-related-posts.title: I Wanna Be With You
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A lost power-pop classic, "I Wanna Be With You" charms with its lovesick loser protagonist, fiercely defiant lyrics and exuberant arrangement.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Where the Bands Are
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "Where the Bands Are" is power pop perfection, showcasing the E Street Band at their most joyous.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Spare Parts: Michael Petrella: Dancing in the Dark/I Wanna Dance With Somebody
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: An unlikely mash-up that works perfectly: Michael Petrella unites one of Bruce Springsteen's greatest hits with one of Whitney Houston's.
